title: Changing agencies and the Savoy house band
summary: He changed agencies, bookings fell, and he got the Savoy house band, which was cut to seven pieces.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, anyway, let's go back to -- to -- so, this second year you could see that bookings were a little different.
Yeah.
Did you say anything?
Well, yeah, I did say something, but that didn't mean nothing. Said they couldn't help it.
Yeah. They just played dumb.
Yeah. So then I changed offices and all. (Unintelligible). Another agency sprung up. And I went with them.
Who?
It was the Ben Bart Agency.
Oh, yeah. Universal.
Universal.
Yeah.

I went with them. And they were strictly colored, you know. Dinah Washington, I think they had. And it didn't do no good. In fact, things started to dropping. And eventually, I got the house band at the Savoy. I had the house band in the Savoy until they closed it down.
Well, Cootie, the Gale Agency wasn't going to give you the house band in the Savoy unless you were back with them, were they?
No, I had the house band in the Savoy.
Well, were you being handled by them?
Yeah. No, I wasn't handled by them then. I tell you, I was working in the Savoy all the time, you know, with the Gale Agency.
Yeah.
I had built up a big reputation at the Savoy Ballroom.
Yeah.
So they needed me up there.
Yeah. They had to have a band that could draw and that could mean something.
Yeah. And produce.
Yeah.
And I had that type of band. So they cut my band down to seven pieces. Okay, cut it down to seven
pieces. Things was bad there. Then I stayed there till they tore it down, with seven pieces.
